title: Hormone Replacement Therapy: Risk-Benefit Counselling and Prescribing Review

evidenceAudit.scope: Woman considering or taking hormone replacement therapy (HRT): risk and benefit counselling for cardiovascular disease, venous thromboembolism and breast cancer, route choice, endometrial protection and review, using NICE NG23.
findings: Every dose, threshold and timing was checked against the cited source section on 2026-10-18.
Normal values are typical adult reference ranges; laboratories differ.
unverifiedSections: NICE NG23 as extracted gives no HRT doses, preparations or switching rules.
Relative risk numbers for breast cancer and VTE and the duration limit beyond 5 years were not captured.
Source pages were read through automated page extraction rather than page-by-page in the original documents, so each figure should be spot-checked against the source during clinical review.
The Saudi Food and Drug Authority (SFDA) drug registration site could not be opened from this environment, so registration of each medicine was not verified; check hospital formulary.

pathophysiology.summary: HRT does not increase cardiovascular disease risk when started in women aged under 60 years. Oestrogen with progestogen HRT can be associated with an increased risk of breast cancer; the risk with transdermal HRT at standard doses is no greater than baseline population risk. VTE risk with HRT is greater for oral than transdermal preparations. Women with a uterus need progestogen for endometrial protection.
keyMechanisms: HRT does not increase cardiovascular disease risk when started in women aged under 60 years.
Oestrogen with progestogen HRT can be associated with an increased risk of breast cancer; the risk with transdermal HRT at standard doses is no greater than baseline population risk.
VTE risk with HRT is greater for oral than transdermal preparations.
Women with a uterus need progestogen for endometrial protection.

clinicalManagement.title: Counsel on risks and benefits
actions: Discuss short-term (up to 5 years) and longer-term benefits and risks.

clinicalManagement.title: Choose regimen and route
actions: Oestrogen with progestogen for women with a uterus; oestrogen alone without; transdermal for increased VTE risk.

clinicalManagement.title: Add vaginal oestrogen if needed
actions: Offer vaginal oestrogen, including to women on systemic HRT.

clinicalManagement.title: Review
actions: Assess efficacy, tolerability and bleeding; give contraception information.

medicationPlan.note: NICE NG23 gives no HRT doses or product choices. Drug, dose and switching follow the menopause service protocol and product information. The Saudi Food and Drug Authority (SFDA) drug registration site could not be opened from this environment, so registration of each medicine was not verified; check hospital formulary.
